title: Forgot password or locked out
text: Go to the Northbridge password reset page and choose Forgot my password.
why: Self-service reset fixes this in minutes without waiting for a technician.
confirm: Did you open the reset page?

title: Forgot password or locked out
text: Verify your identity with the method on your phone, then choose a new password.
why: Verification protects your account from someone pretending to be you.
confirm: Did you verify and set a new password?

title: Forgot password or locked out
text: You no longer have access to any verification method.

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
text: I know the Wi-Fi network name and password
why: One step has you forget the network and sign back in.

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
why: A later step restarts the computer.

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
text: Click the network icon on the taskbar and make sure Wi-Fi is on and Airplane mode is off.
why: A switched-off adapter or Airplane mode is the most common cause, and the fastest to rule out.
confirm: Did you check that Wi-Fi is on and Airplane mode is off?

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
text: Open Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks, select your network, choose Forget, then reconnect and enter the password.
why: A saved network profile can go stale after a password or router change. Rejoining creates a fresh one.
confirm: Did you forget the network and reconnect with the password?

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
text: Check whether another device (your phone, for example) can connect to the same Wi-Fi.
why: If no device can connect, the problem is the network, not your computer.
confirm: Did you test the Wi-Fi on another device?

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
why: A restart reloads the network adapter and clears temporary errors.
confirm: Did you restart and try connecting again?

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
text: Open Settings > Windows Update and install any available updates, then restart.
why: Updates often include fixed network adapter drivers.
confirm: Did you install updates and restart?

title: Wi-Fi won't connect (Windows 10 or 11)
text: No other device can connect either, or none of the steps worked.
